overview: After 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 White plays 3.g3, a fianchetto anti-Sicilian, and Black answers with the flank thrust 3...b5, aiming for ...Bb7 against e4 and queenside space. White can answer with Bg2, d3 and O-O, or a4 to undermine the b5 pawn. Rare line; I am unsure how much material is really given.

white_ideas.idea: Complete the fianchetto with Bg2 and d3, castle and target the b5 pawn with a4.
Control e4 with d3 and Nbd2 and avoid the long diagonal weaknesses.

black_ideas.idea: Use the a-pawn and queenside for space; ...b4 to gain squares.

typical_structures.structure: Closed-Sicilian-like set-up with White g3 and Bg2 against Black b5/c5 pawn chain.

character.notes: Flank play with sensible development; the b5 thrust is committal but not explosive.

gambit.notes: Despite the name, I do not see a pawn White can force away, so I tag no gambit with low confidence.

soundness.notes: The ...b5 thrust is playable and not obviously refuted.

structure.notes: Sicilian asymmetric centre with a half-open file.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play ...b5 here; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Rare and uncommon set-up; Black's plans are not obvious.
